He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]] and the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==High school career== Green attended [[Saints John Neumann and Maria Goretti Catholic High School]] in [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]], where he won four consecutive Pennsylvania Class 3A state championships. Green finished his career at Neumann-Goretti with 1,853 points, which ranks second in program history. In 2016, Green played in the summer for the PSA Cardinals in the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|Nike EYBL]] and helped lead his team to a berth in the 2016 Nike Peach Jam. He was named to the All-EYBL first team after averaging 14.1 points and 10.5 assists. In January 2017, Green was selected as a [[McDonald's All-American]].{{cite web|last1=USA Today|title=Quade Green bucking the diet for the golden arches after receiving McDonald's All American jersey|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2017/quade-green-bucking-the-diet-for-the-golden-arches-after-receiving-mcdonalds-all-american-jersey|website=USA Today High School Sports|access-date=June 5, 2017|date=January 23, 2017}} Green won the Legends and Stars Shootout competition during the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017 McDonald's All-American Game]]. In February 2017, Green was selected to participate in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite web|last1=USA Today|title=Kentucky signee Quade Green honored at Jordan Brand Classic Senior Night|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2017/kentucky-signee-quade-green-honored-at-jordan-brand-classic-senior-night|website=USA Today High School Sports|date=February 15, 2017}} ===Recruiting=== On November 16, 2016, Green committed to attend and play for the [[University of Kentucky]].{{cite web|last1=ESPN|title=Kentucky lands five-star point guard Quade Green|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/18091170/kentucky-wildcats-get-five-star-point-guard-quade-green|website=ESPN|access-date=June 5, 2017|date=November 20, 2016}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Quade Green | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, PA]] | highschool = [[Saints John Neumann and Maria Goretti Catholic High School|Neumann–Goretti]] (PA) | feet = 6 | inches = 1 | weight = 170 | 40 = | commitdate = November 16, 2016 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 92 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = Kentucky 2017 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2017 Kentucky Wildcats Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = kentucky | 247 school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = 96 | scout overall = 24 | rivals overall = 22 | 247 overall = 33 | espn overall = 24 | accessdate = June 21, 2017 | bball = yes }} ==College career== As a freshman, Green posted 9.3 points and 2.7 assists per game while shooting 37.6 percent from behind the arc. He started 13 of the first 14 games before missing three straight games due to injury. He moved to a bench role after returning from injury. Green scored in double figures eight times in 20 games after returning. Green returned to Kentucky for his sophomore season despite rumors of transferring. On December 11, he announced he would be transferring from the University of Kentucky. On January 4, 2019, he was welcomed to the [[University of Washington]] basketball program.{{cite web|title=Washington Officially Adds Quade Green to the Husky Family|url=https://gohuskies.com/news/2019/1/4/mens-basketball-washington-officially-adds-quade-green-to-the-husky-family.aspx|website=GoHuskies|access-date=January 4, 2019}} In January 2020 it was announced that Green was ruled academically ineligible for the winter quarter and could possibly return for the postseason. He averaged 11.6 points, 5.3 assists, 2.6 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 51.4 percent from the floor and 44.7 percent from 3-point range in 15 games.{{cite news |last1=Hines |first1=Travis |title=Report: Washington's Quade Green academically ineligible |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/01/09/report-washingtons-quade-green-academically-ineligible/ link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} ==National team career== Green was named to the 2017 USA Junior National Select Team that played in the 20th annual Nike Hoop Summit but was unable to play in the game due to injury. Green won a gold medal with USA Basketball at the 2016 FIBA Americas U18 Championship. Green averaged 4.6 points, 2.6 assists, and 1.8 rebounds in five games.
